reporting-org.narrative: Kenya National Commission on Human Rights

title.narrative: Protection and Promotion of Human Rights and Fundamental Freedoms for refugees and host communities

description.narrative: To enhance the protection, promotion, and realization of human rights and fundamental freedom of the refugees and host communities in Kenya

participating-org.narrative: Kenya National Commission on Human Rights

title.narrative: Duty bearers and stakeholders (CUC, Committee & working group members) trained on HRBA application to refugees and host communities

description.narrative: Targeted capacity building of key duty bearers involved in refugee management is critical in the overall enjoyment and upholding the rights of refugees. This grant supports training of police officers, judicial officers and refugee technical working groups

title.narrative: Number of duty key bearers trained on HRBA application to refugees and host communities’ matters

description.narrative: This indicator measures the number of duty bearers who have received training on application of Human Rights-Based Approach (HRBA) to matters concerning refugees and host communities. It also tracks the quantity of duty key bearers, such Law Enforcement Agents , CUC members , Refugee Committee members and Working groups who have undergone training specifically focused on integrating human rights principles into their work with refugees and host communities

comment.narrative: The capacity of 132 law enforcement officers was enhanced on refugee rights, refugee approved documentations and the application of Human Rights Based Approach in discharging their duties especially when handling refugee matters. Additionally, A total of 5 CUC trainings were conducted in Garissa, Dadaab, Nairobi, Mombasa, Lodwar, Eldoret and Kakuma reaching 307 stakeholders mainly police officers, immigration officials, prison officers, civil society organisations and justice actors. Other trainings and engagements undertaken were; 4 Gender TWG held reaching 66 participants from state and non-state actors, 2 Mental Health TWG held directly impacting 42 participants and 1 partner meeting on migration management conducted attracting 22 partners representatives.

title.narrative: Victims of human rights violations provided with appropriate redress and resolution of complaints

description.narrative: The KNCHR in line with its statutory and constitutional mandate receive and process complaints on alleged human rights violations. Complaints that fall within the KNCHR’s mandate are subjected to further analysis and follow up that includes among others investigations. Complaints that fall outside the KNCHR’s mandate are referred to relevant complaints handling institutions for further action.

title.narrative: Number of Cases received and processed

description.narrative: The total number of human rights complaints received, processed and documented by the KNCHR

comment.narrative: During the reporting period a total of 859 complaints were received and processed as per the entries in the Complaint management systems as at the end of the second year of the project. Of the total cases recorded, 570 were male, 278 female and 1 intersex. 28 were Persons with Disabilities. Violations on Civil and Political Rights formed the highest number of complaints received accounting for 429 (49.9%) followed by Economic and Social Rights 280 (32.6%) and Group rights 150 (17.5%). Out of these cases, 126 were received from refugees while 733 were from the host community

title.narrative: Number of cases resolved through Alternative Dispute Resolution

description.narrative: This indicator measures the number of cases resolved through Alternative Dispute Resolution (ADR), specifically within the recommended time frame set by the Kenya National Commission on Human Rights (KNCHR) and the Refugee Consortium of Kenya (RCK). It tracks the quantity of cases successfully resolved through non-adversarial methods, such as mediation or negotiation, promoting timely and efficient resolution of human rights disputes outside of formal court processes.

comment.narrative: The project facilitated the training and certification of 35 (21M, 14 F) professional mediators, drawn from refugee and host communities on use of ADR in resolving human rights cases in Kakuma in November 2024. Leveraging on the knowledge and capacity strengthening of the trainees, there was an increase in the number of cases being resolved through ADR. A total of 8 human rights cases were successfully processed through ADR; 2 of which were done by a refugee trained mediator.

title.narrative: Number of PILs undertaken to affirm human rights

description.narrative: This indicator will measure the number of Public Interest Litigations (PILs) undertaken to affirm human rights. It tracks the quantity of legal cases filed on behalf of the public or marginalized groups to protect and assert human rights. The indicator reflects the level of legal advocacy and litigation efforts aimed at advancing human rights principles and addressing violations through judicial means.

comment.narrative: The Commission insituted a PIL on right to decent work by refugees and successfully filed constitutional petition No. E554/2025: KNCHR & KITUO CHA SHERIA v CS INTERIOR & OTHERS, which will, among other things, seek a declaration that the administrative hurdles placed on refugees during the work permit application process are unconstitutional. The matter is currenly ongoing in a law court. Further, the commission undertook additional 8 court interventions on unlawful arrest of refugees, defilement, violation of right to life, and delays in RSD process.

title.narrative: Refugees and host communities trained and sensitized on rights and fundamental freedoms and participate in decision making processes and peacebuilding

description.narrative: The grants supports a rights awareness program through trainings, celebration of thematic human rights days, media campaigns, use of IEC materials, bulk sms and community forums of rights holders (Refugees and Host communities) to enhance their ability to claim their rights. This intervention aims to lead to their increased understanding of human rights, their duties and responsibilities, the refugee act 2021 and other relevant policies, importance of integration as well as the mandates of different institutions managing their affairs in the country.

title.narrative: Number of refugees & Host Communities trained on human rights, refugee law and peace building

description.narrative: This indicator measures the number of refugees & Host Communities trained on human rights, refugee law and peace building.

comment.narrative: A total of 9 training training workshops conducted which built the capacity building of 546 rights holders (Refugees and Host communities) on rights awareness, HRBA, Refugee Act 2021 and enhancing their ability to claim their rights. One notable indicator of success during this period was the active involvement of previously trained (year 1) ToTs as facilitators for new sessions. This internal rotation demonstrated a successful transfer of knowledge and skills, proving that the project is effectively building self-reliance and local expertise within the community.

title.narrative: Number of refugees and host communities sensitized on their rights and freedoms, social governance and peacebuilding issues

description.narrative: This indicator documents the total number of refugee and host communities members sensitized on Human rights through awareness forums and celebration of human rights thematic days

comment.narrative: The KNCHR reached 7150 refugees and host community members through targeted community forums across all project implementation sites, social media advocacy campaigns, and celebration of human rights thematic awareness days such as International Human Rights Day 2024, International Day of Peace and World Refugee Day 2025. The participants noted improved relationship and peaceful co-existence between the refugees and host community.

title.narrative: Strengthened Legal Framework and enhanced Advocacy for Refugee and Host Community Rights

description.narrative: This indicator will measure the number and quality of advocacy interventions developed and lobbying sessions held to promote the inclusion of refugees in national and county-level laws and development plans, such as County Integrated Development Plans (CIDPs) and operationalization of Refugee Status Appeal Committe (RSAC)

title.narrative: Number and quality of advocacy interventions developed and undertaken for the inclusion of refugees in national and county level laws and development plans e.g. CIDPs

description.narrative: The total number of advocacy sessions conducted with key stakeholders in refugee management

comment.narrative: The Project team undertook 3 advocacy sessions; one with National assembly committee on justice, legal affairs and human rights and the other two with Garissa County government which hosts Daadab Refugee camp. The sessions advanced refugee protection, governance and inclusion in policy development

title.narrative: Number of lobbying sessions & action plans developed for the establishment and operationalization of the Refugee Status Appeals Committee

description.narrative: This indicator measures the number of lobbying sessions held and action plans developed for the establishment and operationalization of the Refugee Status Appeals Committee, the Refugee Advisory Committee, and Parliamentary committees related to refugee matters

comment.narrative: A partnership meeting was held between the Commission and DRS leadership to deliberate on the issue of access to services for refugees, multi-agency screening of asylum seekers, suspension of registration of asylum seekers from Eritrea and Ethiopia as well as revocation of refugees’ status of 3 South Sudanese Refugees. Through the said meeting, the partnership between the two agencies were strengthened, joint follow-up activities were agreed upon, a detailed legal opinion from the Commission on the revocation of status for south Sudanese Refugees was prepared and shared.

title.narrative: Refugees & host communities accessing mental health and psychosocial support services

description.narrative: Through this output, the project will contribute to the well-being and resilience of refugees, host communities and duty bearers especially police officers in Kenya, by addressing the mental health and psychosocial consequences of displacement and providing legal assistance. The refugees and host communities will have increased access to legal aid and quality MHPSS services, which will be delivered through community-based approaches that are sensitive to cultural and gender-specific needs.

title.narrative: Number of refugees and the host communities. sensitized on mental health and trauma management

description.narrative: This indicator measures the number of refugees and host communities who have participated in sensitization programs focused on mental health and trauma management. It tracks the quantity of individuals who receive targeted awareness and education sessions to enhance their understanding of mental health issues, trauma, and strategies for coping and recovery.

comment.narrative: 14 psychoeducation forums conducted reaching 745 (312M,433F) refugees and host communities across Nairobi, Garissa, Nairobi, Kakuma. These sessions were instrumental in reducing mental health stigma in the community, highlighting the link between mental health and conflict, and led to improved health seeking behavior on mental health issues as evidenced by the increased number of community members taking mental health services from the project's MHPSS team.

title.narrative: Number of police officers who attended the debriefing sessions

description.narrative: This indicator will measure the number of police officers reached through debriefing sessions

comment.narrative: 8 police training conducted to police officers from Ifo and Dagahaley police stations jointly, Mwingi, Kitui Kithimani, Garissa, Madogo, Iftin, Kakuma and Nairobi reaching 282 (239M,43W) police officers. As a result, the officers committed to establishing peer support systems and strengthening existing mental health councils through continued collaboration with the project MHPSS team and other professionals.

title.narrative: Number of refugees & host communities that have access to adequate mental health and psychosocial support

description.narrative: This indicator will measure the number of refugees and host communities who have access to sufficient mental health and psychosocial support services. It will track the quantity of individuals who receive appropriate assistance, counseling, and resources to address their mental health needs and promote their psychosocial well-being.

comment.narrative: The project team in Garissa, Nairobi, Kakuma and Dadaab conducted individual counselling sessions and psychosocial support to group, family and couples throughout the reporting period reaching 560 refugees and host community members in need of mental health services.
